newsitem.title: UK: EU backs UK proposal for jobs chapter wording-Cook.
newsitem.headline: EU backs UK proposal for jobs chapter wording-Cook.

text.p: European Union governments have agreed to a British proposal to put labour market flexibility at the core of the bloc's proposed employment chapter, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Monday.
Speaking to parliament, he described the employment chapter as a modest, sensible step that will require EU institutions to consider the consequences for jobs of any policies before they adopted.

"I am pleased to inform the House(of Commons)that, unlike the previous administration, the new Labour government has obtained an amendment to the first article of the employment chapter which recognises that, if we are to increase employment, then we must increase employability and increase the flexibility of the labour market," Cook said.
"Article One of the employment chapter now commits the European Union to promoting a skilled, trained and adaptable workforce and labour markets responsive to economic change," he added.
Prime Minister Tony Blair has put the drive for flexible labour markets at the core of his government's European policy since he was elected in a landslide on May 1.
The employment chapter, drafted as an annex to the social chapter on workplace standards, is due to be agreed at the EU's Amsterdam summit on June 16-17.
